newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Ihlas Finans aims one trln lira '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Turk Ihlas Finans aims one trln lira '96 profit.

text.p: Turkish Islamic finance house Ihlas Finans Kurumu said it targeted a one trillion lira profit at the end of 1996 and 35 trillion lira of deposits.

"By the end of 1996, our institution which will raise the number of its branches to 25, targets to inrease the funds collected (deposits) to 35 trillion lira and make one trillion lira of profits," Mehmet Savas, general manager of Ihlas Finans told a press conference.
The institution's earlier 1996 targets were 25 trillion lira of deposits and 21 branches. The profit target was unchanged.
Ihlas Finans was the second leading with 21 percent share in a total of 122 trillion lira of funds deposited at five Islamist finance houses active in Turkey by end-September.

It gradually expanded its branch network to 20 after being set up in April 1995 and also listed 15 percent of its capital on the Istanbul Stock Exchange in July, becoming the first such institution to go public.
Savas said Ihlas Finans also planned to open its first representative office in Frankfurt, Germany in January 1997.
The institution's first-half net profit stood at 240 billion lira and deposits at 19.8 trillion lira.
A sixth finance house was established in Turkey last week and three more await permission from the Treasury.
